He parts from those who stay behind when he most needs them, answers the caller when he calls "hasten to success," gives his soul in reaching it with the giving of a lover, willingly and generously, and continues the journey by morning and evening. He praises the night journey upon arrival, for the traveller praises the night march only at dawn.

I said:
"At dawn the people praise the night journey,
And at death the people praise the meeting."

By Allah, this is not hard or severe, given this short life, which compared to that abode is like an hour of a day: ﴿As if they, on the day they see what they were promised, had not remained but an hour of a day﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35]. ﴿And the day He gathers them, as if they had not remained but an hour of the day, recognizing one another﴾ [Yunus: 45]. ﴿As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. ﴿And the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear they remained not but an hour﴾ [al-Rum: 55]. ﴿He said: "How long did you remain on earth, counted in years?" They said: "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count." He said: "You remained but a little, if only you had known"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112-114].

If one of us were dragged on his face, protecting himself from thorns and stones, to this life, that would not be much, nor a loss compared with what he is spared.

Alas, for an insight that has witnessed these two lives as they truly are, and for a resolve that prefers the lower over the higher! This is only by the success of the One in whose hands are the reins of all affairs, from whom every thing begins and to whom it returns. He kept back the souls over whom wretchedness prevailed from journeying to this abode, and He drew the hearts for whom the good was previously decreed. He made them stand on the path and made the risks easy for them to ride. So those first wasted the stages of their lives with those who stayed behind, while these traversed the stages of their lives with the travellers. The dust settled, the dust storm rose, and the travellers and those who stayed behind were hidden from one another.

It will soon be cleared away: the doers will prevail, and the falsifiers will lose.

Among the goodness and delight of this life: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No soul dies that has with Allah a good reward which would please it to return to the world and have the world and all that is in it, except the martyr. He wishes to return to the world, because of what he sees of Allah's honour for him," meaning that he may be killed in it a second time.

One of the knowers heard a reciter reciting:
"Life is only in the animal enjoyment of pleasure, as the philosopher says.
The rule of the cup of death is that it makes equal in its sip the dullard and the sharp-minded,
And the ignorant becomes beneath the soil of the earth as the clever one has become beneath it.
So ask the earth about the two of them, if the clear question removes doubt and suspicion."

He said: "May Allah fight him! How intense is his opposition to religion and reason! This is the very enemy of the natural disposition (fitrah), the law (shari'ah), reason, faith, and wisdom. O poor one! Because death makes the righteous and the wicked equal, the knowing and the ignorant equal, and all of them beneath the layers of the soil, must they therefore be equal in their final outcome? Do not people who travel from one land to another, on the road, become equal? Yet when they reach their destination, each one descends into the place prepared for him, and is received differently from his companion on the road. Does not each people have a home, so that each one is seated where he deserves? Is one thing repaid with something and the other with its opposite? Has not one who came to the king with what pleases him been honoured by him, while one who came with what angers him has been punished for it? Has not a caravan arrived at the city, so that some of them dwell in its palaces, gardens, and noble places, while others remain on the roadsides among the dogs? Have not two who came from one mother's womb, one of them attained kingship while the other fell into captivity and hardship?"

As for your saying, "Ask the earth about the two of them": indeed we have asked it, and it informed us that it has gathered their bodies, their corpses, and their joints, not their disbelief and faith, nor their lineages and nobilities, nor their forbearance and folly, nor their obedience and disobedience, nor their certainty and doubt, nor their monotheism and polytheism, nor their injustice and justice, nor their knowledge and ignorance. It informed us about these decayed corpses, these dissolving bodies, and these torn joints, and said: "This is the report of what I possess."

As for the report of those spirits and what they have come to, ask about it the books of the Lord of the worlds, His truthful messengers, and their successors who inherited from them. Ask the Qur'an, for with it is the certain report. Ask the one who brought it, for he is the most knowing of the knowers of that. Ask knowledge and faith, for they are the two accepted witnesses. Ask the intellects and the natural dispositions, for with them is the reality of the report. ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is what they judge﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21].

Exalted is Allah, the Most Wise of judges, above this supposition and reckoning, which is fitting only for the most ignorant of the ignorant.

Then he said: "The one who looks into this subject is of two kinds: a man who looks at things, and a man who looks into things. The first is bewildered by them, for their forms, shapes, and outlines empty his mind and sense, and scatter his thought and heart. His looking at them is with the eye of sensation, and it does not benefit him with the fruit of reflection nor the essence of testing, because when he lacks reflection at first, he lacks choice second.

As for the one who looks into things, his looking leads him to pass from their forms to their realities and what is intended by them, and to what the existence of them required of profound wisdom and complete knowledge. This looking benefits him by distinguishing their ranks, knowing what benefits from what harms, the sound from the sick, the lasting from the perishing, the husk from the kernel. He distinguishes between the means and the end, and between the means of a thing and the means of its opposite. Then he knows that this world is its husk and the Hereafter is its kernel, that this world is the place of sowing and the Hereafter is the time of harvest, that this world is a crossing and a passage, and the Hereafter is the abode of settlement.

When he knows that this world is a path and a passage, he is worthy of preparing provision for his settlement. He then knows that he was not created in this abode to settle and remain forever, but to pass on to another place, which is the dwelling and the resting-place. He knows that man was called to this by every law, on the tongue of every prophet, by every sign and proof. A sign was set up for him regarding it, every example was struck for its sake, and he was alerted to it by his first origin and beginnings, and all his other states, and the states of his food and drink, his earth and sky, such that doubt was removed from him, the clear path was shown to him, the proof was established against him, and he was given the fullest excuse and granted the fullest respite. So it became clear to the one of sound intellect and upright disposition that departing from this place is necessary, that moving from it is a truth beyond doubt, and that there is for him another place for which he was created and prepared. His destination is toward it, and his arrival there is without doubt. And that his present abode is a station of passage, not a station of settlement."

In sum: whoever contemplates the existing things, and is not content with merely looking at them alone, will find them indicating that behind this life there is another life more perfect than it, and that this life, in relation to that one, is like sleep in relation to wakefulness, and like a shadow in relation to the person. He will hear them all calling out with what their Lord, their Creator and their Originator called out: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ [Fatir: 5]. They call out in the tongue of their state what their Lord called out in explicit speech. ﴿And present to them the example of the worldly life: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry stalks scattered by the winds. And Allah is ever Able to do all things﴾ [al-Kahf: 45]. And the Exalted said: ﴿The example of the worldly life is only like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, from what people and livestock eat, until when the earth takes its adornment and is beautified, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it into cut-down stubble as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought﴾ [Yunus: 24]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Know that the worldly life is only play and amusement, adornment, boasting among you, and competition in wealth and children. It is like a rain whose plants please the disbelievers; then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval. And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [al-Hadid: 20]. Then He urged them to race toward the Hereafter, the enduring abode that has no end. He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Hadid: 21].

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 56, verses 90–91 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right.﴾

Most of the exegetes circled around the meaning, and they reported and said sayings from which their distance from the intended meaning is not hidden.

Rather, the meaning of the verse, and Allah knows best, is: "Peace be upon you, O you who departs from the world, being of the companions of the right."

That is, his peace upon you is as one of the companions of the right, who are safe from the troubles and distresses of this world, and from the Fire and its punishment.

So he is given good news of safety at his departure from the world and his arrival before Allah, just as the angel gives good news to his soul when taking it, saying: "Rejoice in rest and provision and a Lord not angry."

And this is the first of the good news that the believer receives in the Hereafter.

(Section)

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right﴾,

this is not a greeting of peace (salam tahiyyah). Had it been a greeting, He would have said "Peace be upon him," as He said: ﴿Peace be upon Abraham﴾, ﴿Peace be upon Noah﴾.

Rather, the verse includes mention of the ranks and divisions of people at the Lesser Resurrection (al-qiyamah al-sughra), at the time of arriving before Allah. He mentioned that they are three categories: one brought near, for whom is rest and provision and the Garden of bliss; and one of the companions of the right, for whom is safety, so He promised him safety; and He promised the one brought near spoils and success. Each of them is safe and victorious. And one who is a wrongdoer by his denial and misguidance, He threatened him with an accommodation of boiling water and the burning of Hellfire. Since the situation was not one of greeting, but a report of his state, He mentioned what he attains of safety.

If it is said: "This is a correct distinction, but what is the meaning of the lam in His saying (lak, 'for you'), and who is the one addressed by this address, and what is the meaning of the particle min in His saying: ﴿of the companions of the right﴾?

These are three questions in the verse."

It is said: We have, praise be to Allah, fulfilled the point by mentioning the difference between this peace in the verse and the greeting of peace, which was the intended matter. These questions, although connected to the verse, are outside our purpose. But we answer them to complete the benefit, by the power and strength of Allah. Although we have not seen any of the exegetes who satisfied the thirst in this place or uncovered the reality of the meaning and wording. Rather, some of them say the meaning is "so peace is yours, that you are of the companions of the right," and others say other things that are circling around its meaning without transmission. So know that the thing invoked, of good or evil, is attributed to its owner by the lam of attribution, which indicates that it is his. Among this is His saying: ﴿Those, for them is the curse﴾, and He did not say "upon them the curse," indicating the realization of its meaning and its establishment for them. Likewise His saying: ﴿And for you is woe because of what you describe﴾.

And in the opposite of this one says: "for you is mercy," "for you is greeting," "for you is peace," and among it is this verse: ﴿so peace is for you﴾, meaning peace is established for you and attained by you. On this basis, the address is to everyone who is of this kind, so it is an address to the genus: "So peace is for you, O you who are of the companions of the right," just as you say "congratulations to you, O you who are of them."

For this reason, and Allah knows best, He brought the particle min in His saying: ﴿of the companions of the right﴾, and the prepositional phrase is in the position of a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: "peace is for you, being of the companions of the right," just as you say "congratulations to you, being of the followers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his party," meaning being of them. And a prepositional phrase after a definite noun is put in the accusative as a state, just as you say "I love you, being of the people of religion and knowledge," meaning being of them. This is the meaning of this verse. And although the books of the exegetes are empty of it, some of them have circled around it, and what was transmitted did not uncover the meaning nor clarify it. So review what they said, and Allah the Granter of success is the Bestower by His grace.

[Issue: The Resting Place of Souls]

This is: where is the resting place of the souls between death and the Day of Resurrection? Are they in heaven or on earth? Are they in the Garden or not? And are they deposited in bodies other than their bodies which they were in, so that they are blessed and punished in them, or do they remain disembodied?

This is a great issue about which people spoke and disagreed. It is received only from revelation (al-sam'), and there was disagreement about it. Some said: the souls of the believers are with Allah in the Garden, whether they were martyrs or not, if no major sin or debt prevents them from the Garden, and their Lord meets them with pardon and mercy. This is the view of Abu Hurayrah and Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them.

A group said: they are at the courtyard of the Garden, at its gate, and its spirit, bliss and provision come to them.

A group said: the souls are at the courtyards of their graves.

Malik said: "It has reached me that the soul is released, going wherever it wishes."

(And) Imam Ahmad said in the narration of his son Abdullah: the souls of the disbelievers are in the Fire, and the souls of the believers are in the Garden.

(And) Abu Abdullah ibn Mandah said: A group of the Companions and the Successors said: the souls of the believers are with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they added nothing to that. He said: It is narrated from a group of the Companions and the Successors that the souls of the believers are at al-Jabiyah, and the souls of the disbelievers are at Barhut, a well in Hadramawt.

Safwan ibn Amr said: I asked Amir ibn Abdullah Abu al-Yaman: "Is there a gathering place for the souls of the believers?"

He said: "The land of which Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾"

He said: It is the land to which the souls of the believers gather until the Resurrection. And they said: it is the land which Allah will inherit to the believers in this world.

Ka'b said: the souls of the believers are in 'Illiyyun in the seventh heaven, and the souls of the disbelievers are in Sijjin in the seventh earth, under the army of Iblis.

A group said: the souls of the believers are at the well of Zamzam, and the souls of the disbelievers at the well of Barhut.

Salman al-Farisi said: the souls of the believers are in a barzakh of the earth, going wherever they wish, and the souls of the disbelievers are in Sijjin. In another wording from him: the breath of the believer goes in the earth wherever it wishes.

A group said: the souls of the believers are on the right of Adam, and the souls of the disbelievers on his left.

Another group, including Ibn Hazm, said: their resting place is where they were before their bodies were created.

He said: What we say about the resting place of the souls is what Allah the Mighty and Majestic and His Prophet (ﷺ) said, and we do not go beyond it. It is the clear proof, which is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] – lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."﴾

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had certainly created you and then fashioned you; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam."﴾

So it is established that Allah the Exalted created the souls as a whole. Likewise the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that the souls are mobilized armies: whatever recognizes each other among them is in accord, and whatever is strange to each other differs.

Allah took their covenant and their testimony to His lordship, while they were created, formed, and rational, before He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam and before He placed them into bodies. The bodies at that time were dust and water. Then He settled them where He willed, which is the barzakh to which they return at death. Then He continues to send forth from them group after group, breathing them into the bodies produced from the seed, until he said: So it is established that the souls are bodies carrying their accidents of recognition and rejection, that they are knowing and distinguishing. Allah tests them in this world as He wills, then He takes them back, and they return to the barzakh in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them on the night he was taken up, at the lowest heaven: the souls of the people of happiness on the right of Adam and the souls of the people of wretchedness on his left. That is at the limit of the elements, and He hastens the souls of the prophets and martyrs to the Garden.

He said: Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi mentioned from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh that he mentioned exactly what we have said, and he said: "Upon this the people of knowledge have agreed."

Ibn Hazm said: it is the saying of all the people of Islam. He said: And this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So the companions of the right – what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left – what are the companions of the left? And the forerunners, the forerunners. Those are the ones brought near, in Gardens of Bliss. A company of the former peoples, and a few of the later peoples.﴾

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for if he was of those brought near, then rest and provision and a Garden of bliss﴾ to its end.

So the souls remain there until the number of all souls is complete by their being breathed into bodies; then by their return to the barzakh, the Hour will be established, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic will return the souls to their bodies again. That is the second life, in which the creation is judged: a group in the Garden, and a group in the Blaze, abiding forever. End.

Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr said: the souls of the martyrs are in the Garden, and the souls of the general believers are at the courtyards of their graves. We shall mention his words and what he argued with, and clarify what is in it.

(And) Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ibn Jurayj, in what was read to him from Mujahid: "They are not in the Garden, but they eat of its fruits and find its fragrance."

Mu'awiyah ibn Salih mentioned from Sa'id ibn Suwayd that he asked Ibn Shihab about the spouses of believers, and he said: "It has reached me that the souls of the martyrs are like green birds hanging from the Throne, going and coming to the meadows of the Garden, coming to their Lord every day and greeting Him."

(And) Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr, in explaining the hadith of Ibn Umar: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening; if he is of the people of the Garden, then of the people of the Garden; and if he is of the people of the Fire, it is said to him: 'This is your seat until Allah resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection.'" He said: Those who went to the view that the souls are at the courtyards of graves have used it as evidence, and it is the most sound of what was said on this matter, and Allah knows best, because the reports on this are better in transmission and more established in narration than others.

He said: "The meaning, in my view, is that they are at the courtyards of their graves, not that they are bound to them and never leave the courtyards of graves, as Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it has reached us that the souls roam wherever they wish."

He said: And from Mujahid that he said: "The souls are at the courtyards of the graves for seven days from the day the dead person is buried, not leaving that. And Allah knows best."

A group said: their resting place is pure non-existence (al-'adam al-mahd). This is the saying of those who say that the soul is an accident of the body, like its life and perception, so it ceases with the death of the body just as all accidents conditioned by its life cease. This is a view contrary to the texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah and the consensus of the Companions and Successors, as we will mention, if Allah wills. The point is that, according to this misguided group, the resting place of souls after death is pure non-existence.

A group said: their resting place after death is other souls which are suited to their characters and attributes acquired during their lifetime; so each soul goes to the body of an animal resembling those souls: the predatory soul goes to the bodies of beasts of prey, the dog-like soul to the bodies of dogs, the animal soul to the bodies of animals, and the base and lowly soul to the bodies of insects. This is the saying of the metempsychotics (al-mutanasikhah), deniers of the Return, and it is a saying outside all the sayings of the people of Islam.

This is what has been compiled for me from gathering the sayings of people regarding the destination of their souls after death, and you will not find it collected in one book except this one, definitively. We will mention what supports each saying, what is for each and what is against it, and what is correct among that which the Book and the Sunnah indicate, according to our method which Allah has favored us with; and help and success are hoped for from Him.

[Section: The Place of the Soul]

As for the one who said it is the Garden, he argued with His saying: ﴿And as for if he was of those brought near, then rest and provision and a Garden of bliss﴾.

He said: This was mentioned by Him, glory be to Him, after the mention of its departure from the body by death, and He divided the souls into three categories:

Those brought near: and He informed that they are in the Garden of bliss.

Companions of the right: He judged them to be Muslims, which includes their safety from punishment.

And the deniers, the misguided: and He informed that for them is an accommodation of boiling water and the burning of Hellfire. They said: this is definitely after its separation from the body. And He, glory be to Him, mentioned its state on the Day of Resurrection at the beginning of the surah, so He mentioned its state after death and after resurrection. They argued with His saying: ﴿O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Garden.﴾

And many of the Companions and Successors said that this is said to it at its departure from the world, the angel giving it good news of that. And the saying of the one who said this is said to it in the Hereafter does not contradict this, for it is said to it at death and at resurrection, and this is among the good news of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast – the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of the Garden which you were promised."﴾

And this descent occurs at death, occurs in the grave, and occurs at resurrection, and the first good news of the Hereafter is at death.

It has preceded in the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Azib that the angel says to it at its seizing: "Rejoice in rest and provision," and this is from the provision of the Garden.

And they argued with what Malik narrated in the Muwatta' from Ibn Shihab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, that his father Ka'b ibn Malik used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The soul of the believer is only a bird hanging on a tree of the Garden until Allah returns it to its body on the day He resurrects it."

Abu Umar said: In Malik's narration of this there is a clarification of al-Zuhri's hearing of this hadith from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik. Likewise Yunus narrated it from al-Zuhri: "I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik narrating from his father," and likewise al-Awza'i narrated from al-Zuhri: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b related to me." Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli has given this hadith a defect, that Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, Muhammad ibn Akhi al-Zuhri and Salih ibn Kaysan narrated it from al-Zuhri from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik from his grandfather Ka'b, so it would be disconnected (munqati'). Salih ibn Kaysan said from Ibn Shihab from Abd al-Rahman that it reached him that Ka'b ibn Malik used to narrate. Al-Dhuhli said: "This is what is preserved with us, and what resembles it is the hadith of Salih, Shu'ayb and the nephew of al-Zuhri." Other memorizers opposed him in this and judged in favor of Malik and al-Awza'i.

Abu Umar said: Malik, Yunus ibn Yazid, al-Awza'i and al-Harith ibn Fudayl agreed on narrating this hadith from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, and al-Tirmidhi and others authenticated it.

(And) Abu Umar said: I see no basis for what Muhammad ibn Yahya said in this, nor any evidence for it. The agreement of Malik, Yunus ibn Yazid, al-Awza'i and Muhammad ibn Ishaq is more worthy of the correct, and the soul is more at ease with their saying, and their narration is more settled; they are of memorization and mastery such that those who opposed them in this hadith cannot be compared with them. End.

Muhammad al-Dhuhli said: I heard Ali ibn al-Madini say: Ka'b had five sons:
Abdullah, Ubaydullah, Ma'bad, Abd al-Rahman, and Muhammad.

Al-Dhuhli said: Al-Zuhri heard from Abdullah ibn Ka'b, who was his father's guide when he went blind, and he heard from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka'b, and he narrated from Bashir ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, and I do not think he heard from him. End.

So the hadith, if it is from Abd al-Rahman from his father from Ka'b as Malik and those with him said, then it is apparent. And if it is from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka'b from his grandfather as Shu'ayb and those with him said, then its end is that it is a mursal from this route and a connected one from the other, and those who connected it are not less than those who sent it, in rank or in number. So the hadith is among the sound hadiths, and the two Sahihs did not include it only because of this defect, and Allah knows best.

(He said) Abu Umar: As for his saying "the soul of the believer" (nasmat al-mu'min), the nasmah here is the soul. This is shown by his saying (ﷺ) in the same hadith: "until Allah returns it to his body on the day He resurrects him." It was said: nasmah is the soul, the self and the body. The origin of this word, namely nasmah, is the human being himself.

And the soul is called nasmah, and Allah knows best, because a person's life is by his soul; when it departs from him, he is nonexistent or becomes like the nonexistent.

The evidence that nasmah means the person is his saying (ﷺ): "And whoever frees a believing nasmah." And the saying of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "By He who split the grain and created the nasmah." And the poet said:

"Greater than you in reckoning is one who is pious, when the nasmat shake off the dust."

Meaning: when people are raised from their graves on the Day of Resurrection. And al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said:

The soul (nasmah) is the human being. He said: and nasmah is the spirit (rūh), and nasīm is the blowing of the wind. As for His saying, exalted is He, concerning the trees of Paradise, it is narrated with a fatḥah on the lām, which is the more common reading, and it is narrated with a ḍammah on the lām, and the meaning is the same: eating and grazing. It means: it eats of the fruits of Paradise and roams among its trees. The ʿalūqah and ʿalūq mean eating and grazing. The Arabs say: "He did not taste ʿalūqah today," meaning food. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Abī Ziyād said, describing horses:

"And flanked horses that do not taste ʿalūqah, / they suckle with the mares and the foals."

And al-Aʿshā said:

"And a desert, as if its back were the face of a shield, / in which there is nothing but droppings (rajīʿ) and ʿalāq."

I say: From this is the saying of ʿĀʾishah: "The women at that time were light (khifāf), the flesh had not covered them; they would only eat the ʿalaqah of food." The root of the word is from taʿlīq (attachment), which is that food which clings to the heart and soul.

He said: The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this ḥadīth. Some of them said: The souls of the believers are with Allah in Paradise, whether they were martyrs or not, provided that no major sin or debt prevents them from entering Paradise, and their Lord meets them with pardon for them and mercy towards them.

He said: They argued that this ḥadīth did not single out a martyr from a non-martyr.

They also argued with what is related from Abū Hurayrah:

"The souls of the righteous are in ʿIlliyyīn, and the souls of the wicked are in Sijjīn."

And from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr something similar.

Abū ʿUmar said: This is a view opposed by a Sunnah report whose authenticity cannot be disputed, which is his saying:

"When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening: if he is among the people of Paradise, then he is of the people of Paradise; and if he is among the people of the Fire, then he is of the people of the Fire. It is said to him: 'This is your seat, until Allah resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Others said: The meaning of this ḥadīth concerns only the martyrs and not others, because the Qur'an and the Sunnah indicate only that. As for the Qur'an, it is His saying: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for, rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾.

As for the narrations, he mentioned the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, through the route of Baqī ibn Makhlad, traced to the Prophet:

"The martyrs go out in the morning and return in the evening; then their abode is lanterns hung beneath the Throne. The Lord, blessed and exalted, says to them: {Do you know of any honour greater than the honour I have bestowed upon you?} They say: 'No, except that we wish You would return our souls into our bodies, so that we may fight again and be killed in Your way.'" He related it from Hannād, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Mukhtār, from al-Mukhtār, from ʿAṭiyyah, from him.

(Then he related the ḥadīth of) Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "When your brothers were struck (meaning on the day of Uhud), Allah placed their souls in the bellies of green birds that drink from the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and take refuge in lanterns of gold suspended in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food, drink, and resting place, they said: 'Who will convey to our brothers that we are alive in Paradise and provided for, so that they do not shrink from war and lose interest in jihad?' He said: Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'I will convey on your behalf,' and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾."

The ḥadīth is in Musnad Aḥmad and Sunan Abī Dāwūd.

Then he mentioned the ḥadīth of al-Aʿmash from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾

He said: "Indeed, we asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are in the bellies of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take refuge in those lanterns. Your Lord looks upon them with a look, and says: "Do you desire anything?" They say: "What could we desire, when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish!" He did this with them three times. When they saw that they would not stop being asked, they said: "O Lord, we want You to return our souls into our bodies, so that we may be killed in Your way once more." When He saw that they had no need, He left them.'" The ḥadīth is in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

I say: In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from Anas, that Umm al-Rabīʿ bint al-Barāʾ, who is the mother of Ḥārithah ibn Surāqah, came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, will you not tell me about Ḥārithah?" (He had been killed on the day of Badr, struck by a stray arrow.) "If he is in Paradise, I will be patient; and if it is otherwise, I will strive hard in weeping over him." He said: "O Umm Janān, indeed your son has attained the highest Paradise (al-Firdaws al-Aʿlā)."

Then he related, through the route of Baqī ibn Makhlad, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: "The souls of the martyrs roam in the bellies of green birds that hang from the fruit of Paradise."

Then he mentioned: from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: "It has reached us that the souls of the martyrs are in the form of white birds that eat from the fruits of Paradise."

(And through the route of) Abū ʿĀṣim al-Nabīl, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr: "The souls of the martyrs are in birds like the zarāzīr, they recognise one another and are provided with fruit of Paradise."

Abū ʿUmar said: All these reports indicate that they are the martyrs and no others. In some of them it is "in the form of birds," in some "in the bellies of birds," and in some "like green birds." He said:

"And what seems to me, Allah knows best, is that the view of the one who said 'like a bird' or 'in the form of birds' is correct, because it matches our aforementioned ḥadīth (meaning the ḥadīth of Kaʿb ibn Mālik), and his saying in it: 'the soul of the believer is like a bird,' and he did not say 'in the belly of a bird.'"

He said: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus related the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbdullāh: "like green birds."

I say: What is in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim is "in the bellies of green birds."

Abū ʿUmar said: According to this interpretation, it is as if the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed the soul of the believer who is a martyr is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise."

I say: There is no contradiction between his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise," and his saying: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening; if he is among the people of Paradise, then he is of the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of the Fire, then he is of the people of the Fire."

This address includes the dead man on his bed and the martyr, just as his saying: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise" includes the martyr and others. And along with his seat being shown to him morning and evening, his soul is returned to the rivers of Paradise, and eats of its fruits.

As for his specific seat and the house prepared for him, he will enter it only on the Day of Resurrection. What shows this is that the abodes, homes and palaces of the martyrs which Allah prepared for them are definitely not those lanterns in which their souls take refuge in the barzakh. They see their dwellings and seats in Paradise, and their resting place is in those lanterns hung beneath the Throne. The complete and perfect entry occurs on the Day of Resurrection, and the entry of souls into Paradise in the barzakh is a matter below that.

The parallel of this is the people of wretchedness: their souls are presented to the Fire morning and evening; and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they enter their dwellings and seats to which they were presented in the barzakh. So the souls' enjoyment of Paradise in the barzakh is one thing, and their enjoyment together with their bodies on the Day of Resurrection is another. The nourishment of the soul from Paradise in the barzakh is less than its nourishment together with its body on the day of resurrection. Hence his saying: "takes refuge in the trees of Paradise," meaning it eats the ʿalaqah; and the full eating, drinking, clothing and enjoyment occurs only when they are returned to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection. It is evident that nothing in the Sunnah contradicts this view; rather, the Sunnah supports it and agrees with it.

As for the view of the one who said that the ḥadīth of Kaʿb concerns only the martyrs and not others, this is a specification for which the wording contains nothing indicating it, and the general wording applies to its smallest referents: the martyrs, in relation to all believers, are very few. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, attached this reward to the attribute of faith; so it is faith that necessitates it, and he did not attach it to the attribute of martyrdom. Do you not see that the rulings specific to martyrs are attached to the attribute of martyrdom, as in his saying in the ḥadīth of al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib: "The martyr has six qualities with Allah: he is forgiven at the first gush of his blood, he sees his seat in Paradise, he is adorned with the robe of faith, he is married to the houris, he is protected from the punishment of the grave, he is safe from the greatest terror, a crown of dignity is placed on his head, a ruby of which is better than this world and all that is in it, he marries seventy-two houris, and he intercedes for seventy of his relatives." Since this applies specifically to the martyr, he said "for the martyr," and did not say "for the believer." Likewise his saying in the ḥadīth of Qays al-Judhāmī: "The martyr is given six qualities," and likewise all other ḥadīths and texts in which the reward is attached to martyrdom.

As for what the reward is attached to faith, it includes every believer, martyr or non-martyr.

As for the texts and reports mentioned concerning the provision of the martyrs and their souls being in Paradise, they are all true, and they do not indicate the denial of the entry of the souls of other believers into Paradise, especially the truthful ones (al-Ṣiddīqūn), who are the best of the martyrs without dispute among people. So it is said to them: "What do you say about the souls of the truthful ones: are they in Paradise or not?"

If they say they are in Paradise—there is no permissible position for them other than this—then it is established that these texts do not indicate that the souls of martyrs are specifically in that state. If they say they are not in Paradise, it follows for them that the souls of the greatest companions, such as Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān and their like, may Allah be pleased with them, are not in Paradise, while the souls of the martyrs of our time are in Paradise—and this is known to be false by necessity.

If it is said: If this ruling does not apply specifically to martyrs, what is the reason for mentioning them specifically in these texts?

I say: It is to draw attention to the virtue of martyrdom and the elevation of its rank, and that this is guaranteed for its people, and that they certainly have the most abundant share of it. Their share of this bliss in the barzakh is more perfect than the share of other dead people on their beds; and although the dead person on his bed may be higher in rank than them, he has a bliss specific to him which the one below him does not share.

This is supported by the fact that Allah, glory be to Him, placed the souls of martyrs in the bellies of green birds. For when they gave their souls for Allah, to the point that His enemies destroyed them in Him, He compensated them, in the barzakh, with bodies better than them, in which they remain until the Day of Resurrection, and their bliss through those bodies is more perfect than the bliss of disembodied souls. Hence the soul of the believer was in the form of a bird or like a bird, and the soul of the martyr was in the belly of a bird. Consider the wording of the two ḥadīths: he said, "The soul of the believer is a bird," which includes the martyr and others, then he specified the martyr by saying, "and it is in the belly of a bird." It is known that when it is in the belly of a bird, it is truly called a bird. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the one whose words confirm one another, and which show that they are true from Allah.

This combination is better than the combination of Abū ʿAmr and his preference for the report that says "their souls are like green birds"; rather, both reports are true and correct: they are like green birds, and they are in the bellies of green birds.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 56, verses 90–91 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right.﴾

Most of the exegetes circled around the meaning, and they reported and said sayings from which their distance from the intended meaning is not hidden.

Rather, the meaning of the verse, and Allah knows best, is: "Peace be upon you, O you who departs from the world, being of the companions of the right."

That is, his peace upon you is as one of the companions of the right, who are safe from the troubles and distresses of this world, and from the Fire and its punishment.

So he is given good news of safety at his departure from the world and his arrival before Allah, just as the angel gives good news to his soul when taking it, saying: "Rejoice in rest and provision and a Lord not angry."

And this is the first of the good news that the believer receives in the Hereafter.

(Section)

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right﴾,

this is not a greeting of peace (salam tahiyyah). Had it been a greeting, He would have said "Peace be upon him," as He said: ﴿Peace be upon Abraham﴾, ﴿Peace be upon Noah﴾.

Rather, the verse includes mention of the ranks and divisions of people at the Lesser Resurrection (al-qiyamah al-sughra), at the time of arriving before Allah. He mentioned that they are three categories: one brought near, for whom is rest and provision and the Garden of bliss; and one of the companions of the right, for whom is safety, so He promised him safety; and He promised the one brought near spoils and success. Each of them is safe and victorious. And one who is a wrongdoer by his denial and misguidance, He threatened him with an accommodation of boiling water and the burning of Hellfire. Since the situation was not one of greeting, but a report of his state, He mentioned what he attains of safety.

If it is said: "This is a correct distinction, but what is the meaning of the lam in His saying (lak, 'for you'), and who is the one addressed by this address, and what is the meaning of the particle min in His saying: ﴿of the companions of the right﴾?

These are three questions in the verse."

It is said: We have, praise be to Allah, fulfilled the point by mentioning the difference between this peace in the verse and the greeting of peace, which was the intended matter. These questions, although connected to the verse, are outside our purpose. But we answer them to complete the benefit, by the power and strength of Allah. Although we have not seen any of the exegetes who satisfied the thirst in this place or uncovered the reality of the meaning and wording. Rather, some of them say the meaning is "so peace is yours, that you are of the companions of the right," and others say other things that are circling around its meaning without transmission. So know that the thing invoked, of good or evil, is attributed to its owner by the lam of attribution, which indicates that it is his. Among this is His saying: ﴿Those, for them is the curse﴾, and He did not say "upon them the curse," indicating the realization of its meaning and its establishment for them. Likewise His saying: ﴿And for you is woe because of what you describe﴾.

And in the opposite of this one says: "for you is mercy," "for you is greeting," "for you is peace," and among it is this verse: ﴿so peace is for you﴾, meaning peace is established for you and attained by you. On this basis, the address is to everyone who is of this kind, so it is an address to the genus: "So peace is for you, O you who are of the companions of the right," just as you say "congratulations to you, O you who are of them."

For this reason, and Allah knows best, He brought the particle min in His saying: ﴿of the companions of the right﴾, and the prepositional phrase is in the position of a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: "peace is for you, being of the companions of the right," just as you say "congratulations to you, being of the followers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his party," meaning being of them. And a prepositional phrase after a definite noun is put in the accusative as a state, just as you say "I love you, being of the people of religion and knowledge," meaning being of them. This is the meaning of this verse. And although the books of the exegetes are empty of it, some of them have circled around it, and what was transmitted did not uncover the meaning nor clarify it. So review what they said, and Allah the Granter of success is the Bestower by His grace.

[Issue: The Resting Place of Souls]

This is: where is the resting place of the souls between death and the Day of Resurrection? Are they in heaven or on earth? Are they in the Garden or not? And are they deposited in bodies other than their bodies which they were in, so that they are blessed and punished in them, or do they remain disembodied?

This is a great issue about which people spoke and disagreed. It is received only from revelation (al-sam'), and there was disagreement about it. Some said: the souls of the believers are with Allah in the Garden, whether they were martyrs or not, if no major sin or debt prevents them from the Garden, and their Lord meets them with pardon and mercy. This is the view of Abu Hurayrah and Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them.

A group said: they are at the courtyard of the Garden, at its gate, and its spirit, bliss and provision come to them.

A group said: the souls are at the courtyards of their graves.

Malik said: "It has reached me that the soul is released, going wherever it wishes."

(And) Imam Ahmad said in the narration of his son Abdullah: the souls of the disbelievers are in the Fire, and the souls of the believers are in the Garden.

(And) Abu Abdullah ibn Mandah said: A group of the Companions and the Successors said: the souls of the believers are with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they added nothing to that. He said: It is narrated from a group of the Companions and the Successors that the souls of the believers are at al-Jabiyah, and the souls of the disbelievers are at Barhut, a well in Hadramawt.

Safwan ibn Amr said: I asked Amir ibn Abdullah Abu al-Yaman: "Is there a gathering place for the souls of the believers?"

He said: "The land of which Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾"

He said: It is the land to which the souls of the believers gather until the Resurrection. And they said: it is the land which Allah will inherit to the believers in this world.

Ka'b said: the souls of the believers are in 'Illiyyun in the seventh heaven, and the souls of the disbelievers are in Sijjin in the seventh earth, under the army of Iblis.

A group said: the souls of the believers are at the well of Zamzam, and the souls of the disbelievers at the well of Barhut.

Salman al-Farisi said: the souls of the believers are in a barzakh of the earth, going wherever they wish, and the souls of the disbelievers are in Sijjin. In another wording from him: the breath of the believer goes in the earth wherever it wishes.

A group said: the souls of the believers are on the right of Adam, and the souls of the disbelievers on his left.

Another group, including Ibn Hazm, said: their resting place is where they were before their bodies were created.

He said: What we say about the resting place of the souls is what Allah the Mighty and Majestic and His Prophet (ﷺ) said, and we do not go beyond it. It is the clear proof, which is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] – lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."﴾

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had certainly created you and then fashioned you; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam."﴾

So it is established that Allah the Exalted created the souls as a whole. Likewise the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that the souls are mobilized armies: whatever recognizes each other among them is in accord, and whatever is strange to each other differs.

Allah took their covenant and their testimony to His lordship, while they were created, formed, and rational, before He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam and before He placed them into bodies. The bodies at that time were dust and water. Then He settled them where He willed, which is the barzakh to which they return at death. Then He continues to send forth from them group after group, breathing them into the bodies produced from the seed, until he said: So it is established that the souls are bodies carrying their accidents of recognition and rejection, that they are knowing and distinguishing. Allah tests them in this world as He wills, then He takes them back, and they return to the barzakh in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them on the night he was taken up, at the lowest heaven: the souls of the people of happiness on the right of Adam and the souls of the people of wretchedness on his left. That is at the limit of the elements, and He hastens the souls of the prophets and martyrs to the Garden.

He said: Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi mentioned from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh that he mentioned exactly what we have said, and he said: "Upon this the people of knowledge have agreed."

Ibn Hazm said: it is the saying of all the people of Islam. He said: And this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So the companions of the right – what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left – what are the companions of the left? And the forerunners, the forerunners. Those are the ones brought near, in Gardens of Bliss. A company of the former peoples, and a few of the later peoples.﴾

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for if he was of those brought near, then rest and provision and a Garden of bliss﴾ to its end.

So the souls remain there until the number of all souls is complete by their being breathed into bodies; then by their return to the barzakh, the Hour will be established, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic will return the souls to their bodies again. That is the second life, in which the creation is judged: a group in the Garden, and a group in the Blaze, abiding forever. End.

Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr said: the souls of the martyrs are in the Garden, and the souls of the general believers are at the courtyards of their graves. We shall mention his words and what he argued with, and clarify what is in it.

(And) Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ibn Jurayj, in what was read to him from Mujahid: "They are not in the Garden, but they eat of its fruits and find its fragrance."

Mu'awiyah ibn Salih mentioned from Sa'id ibn Suwayd that he asked Ibn Shihab about the spouses of believers, and he said: "It has reached me that the souls of the martyrs are like green birds hanging from the Throne, going and coming to the meadows of the Garden, coming to their Lord every day and greeting Him."

(And) Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr, in explaining the hadith of Ibn Umar: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening; if he is of the people of the Garden, then of the people of the Garden; and if he is of the people of the Fire, it is said to him: 'This is your seat until Allah resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection.'" He said: Those who went to the view that the souls are at the courtyards of graves have used it as evidence, and it is the most sound of what was said on this matter, and Allah knows best, because the reports on this are better in transmission and more established in narration than others.

He said: "The meaning, in my view, is that they are at the courtyards of their graves, not that they are bound to them and never leave the courtyards of graves, as Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it has reached us that the souls roam wherever they wish."

He said: And from Mujahid that he said: "The souls are at the courtyards of the graves for seven days from the day the dead person is buried, not leaving that. And Allah knows best."

A group said: their resting place is pure non-existence (al-'adam al-mahd). This is the saying of those who say that the soul is an accident of the body, like its life and perception, so it ceases with the death of the body just as all accidents conditioned by its life cease. This is a view contrary to the texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah and the consensus of the Companions and Successors, as we will mention, if Allah wills. The point is that, according to this misguided group, the resting place of souls after death is pure non-existence.

A group said: their resting place after death is other souls which are suited to their characters and attributes acquired during their lifetime; so each soul goes to the body of an animal resembling those souls: the predatory soul goes to the bodies of beasts of prey, the dog-like soul to the bodies of dogs, the animal soul to the bodies of animals, and the base and lowly soul to the bodies of insects. This is the saying of the metempsychotics (al-mutanasikhah), deniers of the Return, and it is a saying outside all the sayings of the people of Islam.

This is what has been compiled for me from gathering the sayings of people regarding the destination of their souls after death, and you will not find it collected in one book except this one, definitively. We will mention what supports each saying, what is for each and what is against it, and what is correct among that which the Book and the Sunnah indicate, according to our method which Allah has favored us with; and help and success are hoped for from Him.

[Section: The Place of the Soul]

As for the one who said it is the Garden, he argued with His saying: ﴿And as for if he was of those brought near, then rest and provision and a Garden of bliss﴾.

He said: This was mentioned by Him, glory be to Him, after the mention of its departure from the body by death, and He divided the souls into three categories:

Those brought near: and He informed that they are in the Garden of bliss.

Companions of the right: He judged them to be Muslims, which includes their safety from punishment.

And the deniers, the misguided: and He informed that for them is an accommodation of boiling water and the burning of Hellfire. They said: this is definitely after its separation from the body. And He, glory be to Him, mentioned its state on the Day of Resurrection at the beginning of the surah, so He mentioned its state after death and after resurrection. They argued with His saying: ﴿O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]. And enter among My servants. And enter My Garden.﴾

And many of the Companions and Successors said that this is said to it at its departure from the world, the angel giving it good news of that. And the saying of the one who said this is said to it in the Hereafter does not contradict this, for it is said to it at death and at resurrection, and this is among the good news of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast – the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of the Garden which you were promised."﴾

And this descent occurs at death, occurs in the grave, and occurs at resurrection, and the first good news of the Hereafter is at death.

It has preceded in the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Azib that the angel says to it at its seizing: "Rejoice in rest and provision," and this is from the provision of the Garden.

And they argued with what Malik narrated in the Muwatta' from Ibn Shihab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, that his father Ka'b ibn Malik used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The soul of the believer is only a bird hanging on a tree of the Garden until Allah returns it to its body on the day He resurrects it."

Abu Umar said: In Malik's narration of this there is a clarification of al-Zuhri's hearing of this hadith from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik. Likewise Yunus narrated it from al-Zuhri: "I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik narrating from his father," and likewise al-Awza'i narrated from al-Zuhri: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b related to me." Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli has given this hadith a defect, that Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, Muhammad ibn Akhi al-Zuhri and Salih ibn Kaysan narrated it from al-Zuhri from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik from his grandfather Ka'b, so it would be disconnected (munqati'). Salih ibn Kaysan said from Ibn Shihab from Abd al-Rahman that it reached him that Ka'b ibn Malik used to narrate. Al-Dhuhli said: "This is what is preserved with us, and what resembles it is the hadith of Salih, Shu'ayb and the nephew of al-Zuhri." Other memorizers opposed him in this and judged in favor of Malik and al-Awza'i.

Abu Umar said: Malik, Yunus ibn Yazid, al-Awza'i and al-Harith ibn Fudayl agreed on narrating this hadith from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, and al-Tirmidhi and others authenticated it.

(And) Abu Umar said: I see no basis for what Muhammad ibn Yahya said in this, nor any evidence for it. The agreement of Malik, Yunus ibn Yazid, al-Awza'i and Muhammad ibn Ishaq is more worthy of the correct, and the soul is more at ease with their saying, and their narration is more settled; they are of memorization and mastery such that those who opposed them in this hadith cannot be compared with them. End.

Muhammad al-Dhuhli said: I heard Ali ibn al-Madini say: Ka'b had five sons:
Abdullah, Ubaydullah, Ma'bad, Abd al-Rahman, and Muhammad.

Al-Dhuhli said: Al-Zuhri heard from Abdullah ibn Ka'b, who was his father's guide when he went blind, and he heard from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka'b, and he narrated from Bashir ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, and I do not think he heard from him. End.

So the hadith, if it is from Abd al-Rahman from his father from Ka'b as Malik and those with him said, then it is apparent. And if it is from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka'b from his grandfather as Shu'ayb and those with him said, then its end is that it is a mursal from this route and a connected one from the other, and those who connected it are not less than those who sent it, in rank or in number. So the hadith is among the sound hadiths, and the two Sahihs did not include it only because of this defect, and Allah knows best.

(He said) Abu Umar: As for his saying "the soul of the believer" (nasmat al-mu'min), the nasmah here is the soul. This is shown by his saying (ﷺ) in the same hadith: "until Allah returns it to his body on the day He resurrects him." It was said: nasmah is the soul, the self and the body. The origin of this word, namely nasmah, is the human being himself.

And the soul is called nasmah, and Allah knows best, because a person's life is by his soul; when it departs from him, he is nonexistent or becomes like the nonexistent.

The evidence that nasmah means the person is his saying (ﷺ): "And whoever frees a believing nasmah." And the saying of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "By He who split the grain and created the nasmah." And the poet said:

"Greater than you in reckoning is one who is pious, when the nasmat shake off the dust."

Meaning: when people are raised from their graves on the Day of Resurrection. And al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said:

The soul (nasmah) is the human being. He said: and nasmah is the spirit (rūh), and nasīm is the blowing of the wind. As for His saying, exalted is He, concerning the trees of Paradise, it is narrated with a fatḥah on the lām, which is the more common reading, and it is narrated with a ḍammah on the lām, and the meaning is the same: eating and grazing. It means: it eats of the fruits of Paradise and roams among its trees. The ʿalūqah and ʿalūq mean eating and grazing. The Arabs say: "He did not taste ʿalūqah today," meaning food. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Abī Ziyād said, describing horses:

"And flanked horses that do not taste ʿalūqah, / they suckle with the mares and the foals."

And al-Aʿshā said:

"And a desert, as if its back were the face of a shield, / in which there is nothing but droppings (rajīʿ) and ʿalāq."

I say: From this is the saying of ʿĀʾishah: "The women at that time were light (khifāf), the flesh had not covered them; they would only eat the ʿalaqah of food." The root of the word is from taʿlīq (attachment), which is that food which clings to the heart and soul.

He said: The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this ḥadīth. Some of them said: The souls of the believers are with Allah in Paradise, whether they were martyrs or not, provided that no major sin or debt prevents them from entering Paradise, and their Lord meets them with pardon for them and mercy towards them.

He said: They argued that this ḥadīth did not single out a martyr from a non-martyr.

They also argued with what is related from Abū Hurayrah:

"The souls of the righteous are in ʿIlliyyīn, and the souls of the wicked are in Sijjīn."

And from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr something similar.

Abū ʿUmar said: This is a view opposed by a Sunnah report whose authenticity cannot be disputed, which is his saying:

"When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening: if he is among the people of Paradise, then he is of the people of Paradise; and if he is among the people of the Fire, then he is of the people of the Fire. It is said to him: 'This is your seat, until Allah resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Others said: The meaning of this ḥadīth concerns only the martyrs and not others, because the Qur'an and the Sunnah indicate only that. As for the Qur'an, it is His saying: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for, rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾.

As for the narrations, he mentioned the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, through the route of Baqī ibn Makhlad, traced to the Prophet:

"The martyrs go out in the morning and return in the evening; then their abode is lanterns hung beneath the Throne. The Lord, blessed and exalted, says to them: {Do you know of any honour greater than the honour I have bestowed upon you?} They say: 'No, except that we wish You would return our souls into our bodies, so that we may fight again and be killed in Your way.'" He related it from Hannād, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Mukhtār, from al-Mukhtār, from ʿAṭiyyah, from him.

(Then he related the ḥadīth of) Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "When your brothers were struck (meaning on the day of Uhud), Allah placed their souls in the bellies of green birds that drink from the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and take refuge in lanterns of gold suspended in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food, drink, and resting place, they said: 'Who will convey to our brothers that we are alive in Paradise and provided for, so that they do not shrink from war and lose interest in jihad?' He said: Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'I will convey on your behalf,' and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾."

The ḥadīth is in Musnad Aḥmad and Sunan Abī Dāwūd.

Then he mentioned the ḥadīth of al-Aʿmash from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾

He said: "Indeed, we asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are in the bellies of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take refuge in those lanterns. Your Lord looks upon them with a look, and says: "Do you desire anything?" They say: "What could we desire, when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish!" He did this with them three times. When they saw that they would not stop being asked, they said: "O Lord, we want You to return our souls into our bodies, so that we may be killed in Your way once more." When He saw that they had no need, He left them.'" The ḥadīth is in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

I say: In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from Anas, that Umm al-Rabīʿ bint al-Barāʾ, who is the mother of Ḥārithah ibn Surāqah, came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, will you not tell me about Ḥārithah?" (He had been killed on the day of Badr, struck by a stray arrow.) "If he is in Paradise, I will be patient; and if it is otherwise, I will strive hard in weeping over him." He said: "O Umm Janān, indeed your son has attained the highest Paradise (al-Firdaws al-Aʿlā)."

Then he related, through the route of Baqī ibn Makhlad, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: "The souls of the martyrs roam in the bellies of green birds that hang from the fruit of Paradise."

Then he mentioned: from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: "It has reached us that the souls of the martyrs are in the form of white birds that eat from the fruits of Paradise."

(And through the route of) Abū ʿĀṣim al-Nabīl, from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr: "The souls of the martyrs are in birds like the zarāzīr, they recognise one another and are provided with fruit of Paradise."

Abū ʿUmar said: All these reports indicate that they are the martyrs and no others. In some of them it is "in the form of birds," in some "in the bellies of birds," and in some "like green birds." He said:

"And what seems to me, Allah knows best, is that the view of the one who said 'like a bird' or 'in the form of birds' is correct, because it matches our aforementioned ḥadīth (meaning the ḥadīth of Kaʿb ibn Mālik), and his saying in it: 'the soul of the believer is like a bird,' and he did not say 'in the belly of a bird.'"

He said: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus related the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbdullāh: "like green birds."

I say: What is in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim is "in the bellies of green birds."

Abū ʿUmar said: According to this interpretation, it is as if the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed the soul of the believer who is a martyr is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise."

I say: There is no contradiction between his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise," and his saying: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening; if he is among the people of Paradise, then he is of the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of the Fire, then he is of the people of the Fire."

This address includes the dead man on his bed and the martyr, just as his saying: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs from the trees of Paradise" includes the martyr and others. And along with his seat being shown to him morning and evening, his soul is returned to the rivers of Paradise, and eats of its fruits.

As for his specific seat and the house prepared for him, he will enter it only on the Day of Resurrection. What shows this is that the abodes, homes and palaces of the martyrs which Allah prepared for them are definitely not those lanterns in which their souls take refuge in the barzakh. They see their dwellings and seats in Paradise, and their resting place is in those lanterns hung beneath the Throne. The complete and perfect entry occurs on the Day of Resurrection, and the entry of souls into Paradise in the barzakh is a matter below that.

The parallel of this is the people of wretchedness: their souls are presented to the Fire morning and evening; and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they enter their dwellings and seats to which they were presented in the barzakh. So the souls' enjoyment of Paradise in the barzakh is one thing, and their enjoyment together with their bodies on the Day of Resurrection is another. The nourishment of the soul from Paradise in the barzakh is less than its nourishment together with its body on the day of resurrection. Hence his saying: "takes refuge in the trees of Paradise," meaning it eats the ʿalaqah; and the full eating, drinking, clothing and enjoyment occurs only when they are returned to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection. It is evident that nothing in the Sunnah contradicts this view; rather, the Sunnah supports it and agrees with it.

As for the view of the one who said that the ḥadīth of Kaʿb concerns only the martyrs and not others, this is a specification for which the wording contains nothing indicating it, and the general wording applies to its smallest referents: the martyrs, in relation to all believers, are very few. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, attached this reward to the attribute of faith; so it is faith that necessitates it, and he did not attach it to the attribute of martyrdom. Do you not see that the rulings specific to martyrs are attached to the attribute of martyrdom, as in his saying in the ḥadīth of al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib: "The martyr has six qualities with Allah: he is forgiven at the first gush of his blood, he sees his seat in Paradise, he is adorned with the robe of faith, he is married to the houris, he is protected from the punishment of the grave, he is safe from the greatest terror, a crown of dignity is placed on his head, a ruby of which is better than this world and all that is in it, he marries seventy-two houris, and he intercedes for seventy of his relatives." Since this applies specifically to the martyr, he said "for the martyr," and did not say "for the believer." Likewise his saying in the ḥadīth of Qays al-Judhāmī: "The martyr is given six qualities," and likewise all other ḥadīths and texts in which the reward is attached to martyrdom.

As for what the reward is attached to faith, it includes every believer, martyr or non-martyr.

As for the texts and reports mentioned concerning the provision of the martyrs and their souls being in Paradise, they are all true, and they do not indicate the denial of the entry of the souls of other believers into Paradise, especially the truthful ones (al-Ṣiddīqūn), who are the best of the martyrs without dispute among people. So it is said to them: "What do you say about the souls of the truthful ones: are they in Paradise or not?"

If they say they are in Paradise—there is no permissible position for them other than this—then it is established that these texts do not indicate that the souls of martyrs are specifically in that state. If they say they are not in Paradise, it follows for them that the souls of the greatest companions, such as Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān and their like, may Allah be pleased with them, are not in Paradise, while the souls of the martyrs of our time are in Paradise—and this is known to be false by necessity.

If it is said: If this ruling does not apply specifically to martyrs, what is the reason for mentioning them specifically in these texts?

I say: It is to draw attention to the virtue of martyrdom and the elevation of its rank, and that this is guaranteed for its people, and that they certainly have the most abundant share of it. Their share of this bliss in the barzakh is more perfect than the share of other dead people on their beds; and although the dead person on his bed may be higher in rank than them, he has a bliss specific to him which the one below him does not share.

This is supported by the fact that Allah, glory be to Him, placed the souls of martyrs in the bellies of green birds. For when they gave their souls for Allah, to the point that His enemies destroyed them in Him, He compensated them, in the barzakh, with bodies better than them, in which they remain until the Day of Resurrection, and their bliss through those bodies is more perfect than the bliss of disembodied souls. Hence the soul of the believer was in the form of a bird or like a bird, and the soul of the martyr was in the belly of a bird. Consider the wording of the two ḥadīths: he said, "The soul of the believer is a bird," which includes the martyr and others, then he specified the martyr by saying, "and it is in the belly of a bird." It is known that when it is in the belly of a bird, it is truly called a bird. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the one whose words confirm one another, and which show that they are true from Allah.

This combination is better than the combination of Abū ʿAmr and his preference for the report that says "their souls are like green birds"; rather, both reports are true and correct: they are like green birds, and they are in the bellies of green birds.
